Nova_A 6.0.1 · complete playable project · world-space pointer physics

Build Mouse Knockout from project to portable game

This is an exact, playable workflow—not a list of panel names. The supplied template already implements the complete game, and the manual also explains how to inspect, change, rebuild, test, and export it.

What Nova_A can produce now

Yes. Nova_A can author this game, run it with deterministic fixed-step 2D physics, accept mouse/keyboard/gamepad input, spawn prefab instances, execute Rhai or Visual Graph logic, update UI, and export a standalone player.

On Windows, the Nova_A desktop editor can package the project into a portable x86-64 .exe when the matching Windows player template is installed and Project Health passes. The browser editor can build a web folder, but a browser cannot compile a native .exe. Code signing and clean-machine certification remain separate release-owner steps.

1. Create the ready-to-play project

  1. Launch the Nova_A desktop editor and choose New Project.
  2. Enter a project name such as Mouse Knockout, choose a writable empty folder, and select Mouse Knockout from Templates.
  3. Choose Create Project. The project opens Mouse Knockout Arena as its startup scene and shows Assets/Tutorials/Getting Started.md.
  4. Save once. This establishes the project document before you edit or build it.

2. Prove the game works before editing

  1. Choose Play in the runtime toolbar.
  2. Move the pointer inside the Game view. The blue square follows the pointer in camera/world coordinates; zoom, DPI, and aspect ratio do not change its physical scale.
  3. Hit the eight orange targets. A target counts only after its center and safety margin leave the active camera bounds.
  4. Confirm Score 1 / 8 through Score 8 / 8 and the Congratulations! All targets cleared. bar.
  5. Choose Stop. Play-mode mutations are discarded; authored scene and assets remain unchanged.

3. Understand every supplied object and setting

  • Main Camera — active Camera2D, orthographic size 10, dark background.
  • Mouse Player — visible Rectangle, Kinematic RigidBody2D, BoxCollider2D, restitution 0.7, low friction, and native MouseFollower2D. Maximum speed 40 keeps the response immediate while bounding collision impulses; 0 is the optional unrestricted mode.
  • Game Manager — Script2D with KnockoutGameManager.rhai; resets score, spawns eight targets, checks their camera bounds on a timer, and updates UI.
  • Game HUD — screen-space Canvas at reference size 1920 × 1080.
  • Score Text / Instruction Text — runtime score and player instruction.
  • Congratulations Bar / Congratulations Text — disabled at start and enabled only at 8 / 8.
  • Knockout Target.nova-prefab — Dynamic RigidBody2D with zero scene gravity, restitution 0.86, low friction, BoxCollider2D, and group knockout-target.
  • Scene physics — gravity 0, 60 Hz fixed tick, interpolation enabled. Collision layer 0 interacts with layer 0.

4. Draw or replace an object yourself

  1. Stop Play, open Design, choose the Rectangle drawing tool, then drag in the Scene view. The drag defines actual world width and height.
  2. Select the new object in Hierarchy. In Inspector rename it, set Transform2D position/scale, and verify ShapeRenderer2D plus BoxCollider2D.
  3. For a replacement player, set RigidBody2D → Body type: Kinematic, Gravity scale 0, low friction, then add MouseFollower2D. Keep Offset at 0, 0 and Maximum speed at 40 for responsive, bounded collisions. Use 0 only when you intentionally want unrestricted velocity. Disable or delete the original player only after the replacement passes Play.
  4. For a replacement target, use Body type: Dynamic, Gravity scale 0, restitution about 0.86, low friction, and add it to group knockout-target; it needs no per-target script.
  5. With the target selected, choose Create Prefab in Inspector. Copy its asset://GUID from Assets and replace TARGET_PREFAB_GUID in the manager script.
  6. Keep target size near 1.25 × 1.25 and spawn centers within the Camera2D view so they are visible before play begins.

5. Understand the automatic pointer component and edit the manager script

MouseFollower2D reads the active Game-view pointer in world units and supplies the kinematic velocity inside the native fixed-step loop. This preserves collision response without running a script every frame.

KnockoutGameManager.rhai owns spawning, score, camera-bound checks, destruction, and UI. It checks the grouped targets on a repeating 50 ms timer, so identical per-target scripts are unnecessary. The shipped template contains all eight explicit spawn_at calls; the shortened excerpt below shows the contract.

@export(type="int", min=1, max=64, step=1, group="Game") let remaining = 8;
fn start() {
  score_set(0.0);
  entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Bar"), false);
  entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Text"), false);
  ui_set_text_on(find_entity_handle("Score Text"), "Score  0 / 8");
  spawn_at("asset://TARGET_PREFAB_GUID", -6.0, -3.8, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);
  // Repeat spawn_at at the seven other authored positions.
  timer_start("bounds", 0.05, true);
}
fn on_timer(name) {
  if name != "bounds" || remaining <= 0 { return; }
  let margin = 0.8;
  for target in query_group("knockout-target", 16) {
    let x = entity_position_x_on(target);
    let y = entity_position_y_on(target);
    if x < view_min_x() - margin || x > view_max_x() + margin
      || y < view_min_y() - margin || y > view_max_y() + margin {
      entity_destroy(target); score_add(1.0); remaining = remaining - 1;
    }
  }
  ui_set_text_on(find_entity_handle("Score Text"), `Score  ${8 - remaining} / 8`);
  if remaining == 0 {
    timer_cancel("bounds");
    entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Bar"), true);
    entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Text"), true);
  }
}

6. Configuration checklist before release

  • Project Settings → Physics: fixed tick 60 Hz, finite gravity 0 for this scene, interpolation enabled.
  • Collision Matrix: player and target share an enabled collision pair; UI objects have no physics collider.
  • Input: no custom action is required for pointer position. mouse_world_x/y are read from the active Game view. Keyboard/gamepad actions remain available through Input Map.
  • Camera: exactly one active gameplay Camera2D; orthographic size and viewport determine view_min/max_x/y.
  • Build Settings: Runtime Game, startup scene Mouse Knockout Arena, Target Windows, Architecture x86_64, Package into executable on, identifier such as top.whitelists.mouseknockout, version 1.0.0.
  • Project Health: resolve every Error before Build; warnings for signing or external clean-machine evidence do not change the game logic.

7. Build the portable Windows game

  1. Save the project, then open Manage → Project Health and run validation.
  2. Open Manage → Build Settings → Overview.
  3. Choose Windows, x86_64, runtime Game, and Portable application / Package into executable.
  4. In Scenes, include Mouse Knockout Arena, put it first, and select it as Startup.
  5. Use a Development build for testing or Release for distribution. Keep deterministic packaging enabled.
  6. Choose an output directory outside the source project, then press Build & Run.
  7. Nova_A creates the game data, invokes the matching local player template, writes the portable .exe, and launches it. Copy the resulting executable to another Windows x86-64 machine for the required clean-machine test.
  8. For Web instead, select Web and Web player folder, build, and serve the whole output folder over HTTP(S); do not open index.html through file://.

8. Expected failures and exact fixes

  • Player does not move: pointer must be over the Game view; verify MouseFollower2D is enabled, the body is Kinematic, and there is one active camera.
  • Targets do not move: verify Dynamic body, BoxCollider2D, gravity 0, and that the collision matrix enables layer 0 ↔ 0.
  • Target leaves view but score stays: verify the prefab group is exactly knockout-target, the manager timer is running, and API v2 provides view_min/max.
  • Score changes twice: targets must have the group only once; do not add a second scoring script.
  • Banner never appears: names must be exactly Congratulations Bar, Congratulations Text, and Score Text; remaining must start at the number of spawned targets.
  • Build is unavailable: use the desktop editor on the target host, install/validate the Windows x86-64 export template, select a startup scene, and clear Project Health errors.
Nova_A 6.0.1 · complete playable project · world-space pointer physics

Mouse Knockout vom Projekt bis zum portablen Spiel bauen

Dies ist ein exakter, spielbarer Ablauf und keine Liste von Panelnamen. Die Vorlage enthält das vollständige Spiel; das Handbuch erklärt außerdem Prüfung, Änderung, Neuaufbau, Test und Export.

Was Nova_A jetzt erzeugen kann

Ja. Nova_A kann dieses Spiel erstellen, mit deterministischer 2D-Physik ausführen, Maus/Tastatur/Gamepad lesen, Prefabs erzeugen, Rhai oder Visual Graph ausführen, UI aktualisieren und einen eigenständigen Player exportieren.

Unter Windows erzeugt der Nova_A-Desktop-Editor eine portable x86-64-.exe, wenn die passende Windows-Player-Vorlage installiert ist und Project Health besteht. Der Browser-Editor kann einen Web-Ordner bauen, aber keine native .exe kompilieren. Codesignatur und Prüfung auf einem sauberen Rechner bleiben getrennte Freigabeschritte.

1. Spielbereites Projekt erstellen

  1. Nova_A-Desktop-Editor starten und New Project wählen.
  2. Projektname, etwa Mouse Knockout, und einen beschreibbaren leeren Ordner eingeben; unter Templates Maus-Knockout wählen.
  3. Create Project wählen. Mouse Knockout Arena ist Startszene und Assets/Tutorials/Getting Started.md wird angezeigt.
  4. Einmal speichern, bevor Inhalte geändert oder gebaut werden.

2. Das unveränderte Spiel prüfen

  1. In der Laufzeitleiste Play wählen.
  2. Den Zeiger in der Game-Ansicht bewegen. Das blaue Quadrat folgt in Kamera-/Weltkoordinaten; Zoom, DPI und Seitenverhältnis ändern den Physikmaßstab nicht.
  3. Alle acht orangefarbenen Ziele aus der Ansicht stoßen. Gezählt wird erst außerhalb der Kameragrenze plus Sicherheitsrand.
  4. Score 1 / 8 bis 8 / 8 und danach die Glückwunschleiste prüfen.
  5. Stop wählen. Laufzeitänderungen werden verworfen; Szene und Assets bleiben unverändert.

3. Objekte und Einstellungen der Vorlage

  • Main Camera — aktive Camera2D, Orthografiegröße 10.
  • Mouse Player — Rectangle, kinematischer RigidBody2D, BoxCollider2D, Rückprall 0,7, geringe Reibung und native MouseFollower2D. Höchstgeschwindigkeit 40 reagiert direkt und begrenzt Kollisionsimpulse; 0 bleibt der optionale unbegrenzte Modus.
  • Game Manager — erzeugt acht Ziele, prüft ihre Kameragrenzen per Timer und verwaltet Punktestand und Sieg.
  • Game HUD — bildschirmbezogene Canvas mit 1920 × 1080 Referenz.
  • Score Text / Instruction Text — Punktestand und Anleitung.
  • Congratulations Bar / Congratulations Text — anfangs deaktiviert, bei 8 / 8 aktiviert.
  • Knockout Target.nova-prefab — dynamischer Körper mit Rückprall 0,86, geringer Reibung und Gruppe knockout-target.
  • Szenenphysik — Gravitation 0, 60-Hz-Fixed-Step, Interpolation; Ebene 0 kollidiert mit Ebene 0.

4. Eigenes Objekt zeichnen oder ersetzen

  1. Play stoppen, Design öffnen, das Rectangle-Zeichenwerkzeug wählen und in der Scene-Ansicht ziehen. Die Ziehstrecke bestimmt echte Weltgröße.
  2. Objekt in Hierarchy wählen, im Inspector umbenennen, Transform2D einstellen und ShapeRenderer2D sowie BoxCollider2D prüfen.
  3. Für einen Player RigidBody2D auf Kinematic, Gravity scale 0 und geringe Reibung setzen; MouseFollower2D hinzufügen. Offset 0, 0 und Höchstgeschwindigkeit 40 liefern direkte, begrenzte Kollisionen; 0 nur bewusst für unbegrenzte Geschwindigkeit verwenden. Original erst nach erfolgreichem Play-Test entfernen oder deaktivieren.
  4. Für ein Ziel Dynamic, Gravity scale 0, Rückprall etwa 0,86 und geringe Reibung verwenden und die Gruppe knockout-target hinzufügen; ein eigenes Zielskript ist nicht nötig.
  5. Ziel auswählen, im Inspector Create Prefab wählen, asset://GUID aus Assets kopieren und TARGET_PREFAB_GUID im Manager ersetzen.
  6. Zielgröße etwa 1,25 × 1,25 halten und Spawnpunkte innerhalb der Camera2D-Ansicht setzen.

5. Automatische Zeigerkomponente verstehen und Managerskript bearbeiten

MouseFollower2D liest den Zeiger der aktiven Game-Ansicht in Weltkoordinaten und liefert die kinematische Geschwindigkeit direkt im nativen Fixed-Step. Dadurch bleiben Kollisionen erhalten, ohne pro Frame ein Skript auszuführen.

KnockoutGameManager.rhai verwaltet Spawns, Kameragrenzen, Zerstörung, Punktestand und UI. Es prüft die gruppierten Ziele alle 50 ms, sodass identische Skripte an jedem Ziel entfallen. Die Vorlage enthält acht vollständige spawn_at-Aufrufe; unten steht der verkürzte Vertrag.

@export(type="int", min=1, max=64, step=1, group="Game") let remaining = 8;
fn start() {
  score_set(0.0);
  entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Bar"), false);
  entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Text"), false);
  ui_set_text_on(find_entity_handle("Score Text"), "Score  0 / 8");
  spawn_at("asset://TARGET_PREFAB_GUID", -6.0, -3.8, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);
  // Repeat spawn_at at the seven other authored positions.
  timer_start("bounds", 0.05, true);
}
fn on_timer(name) {
  if name != "bounds" || remaining <= 0 { return; }
  let margin = 0.8;
  for target in query_group("knockout-target", 16) {
    let x = entity_position_x_on(target);
    let y = entity_position_y_on(target);
    if x < view_min_x() - margin || x > view_max_x() + margin
      || y < view_min_y() - margin || y > view_max_y() + margin {
      entity_destroy(target); score_add(1.0); remaining = remaining - 1;
    }
  }
  ui_set_text_on(find_entity_handle("Score Text"), `Score  ${8 - remaining} / 8`);
  if remaining == 0 {
    timer_cancel("bounds");
    entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Bar"), true);
    entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Text"), true);
  }
}

6. Konfiguration vor der Freigabe

  • Project Settings → Physics: 60 Hz, Szenengravitation 0, Interpolation an.
  • Collision Matrix: Player und Ziel besitzen ein aktiviertes Kollisionspaar; UI hat keine Collider.
  • Input: Für den Zeiger ist keine Aktion nötig; mouse_world_x/y liest die aktive Game-Ansicht. Tastatur/Gamepad wird über Input Map konfiguriert.
  • Camera: genau eine aktive Camera2D; Orthografiegröße und Viewport bestimmen view_min/max_x/y.
  • Build Settings: Runtime Game, Startszene Mouse Knockout Arena, Windows, x86_64, Package into executable, Kennung z. B. top.whitelists.mouseknockout, Version 1.0.0.
  • Project Health: alle Fehler vor Build beheben; Signatur- oder externe Testwarnungen verändern die Spiellogik nicht.

7. Portables Windows-Spiel bauen

  1. Projekt speichern und Manage → Project Health validieren.
  2. Manage → Build Settings → Overview öffnen.
  3. Windows, x86_64, Runtime Game und Portable application / Package into executable wählen.
  4. Mouse Knockout Arena aufnehmen, an erste Stelle setzen und als Startup wählen.
  5. Development zum Testen oder Release zur Verteilung; deterministisches Paketieren aktiviert lassen.
  6. Ausgabeordner außerhalb des Quellprojekts wählen und Build & Run drücken.
  7. Nova_A erzeugt Daten, ruft die lokale passende Player-Vorlage auf, schreibt die .exe und startet sie. Danach auf einem anderen Windows-x86-64-Rechner prüfen.
  8. Für Web: Web und Web player folder wählen und den gesamten Ordner über HTTP(S) bereitstellen, nicht über file://.

8. Fehler und genaue Korrekturen

  • Player bewegt sich nicht: Zeiger über Game-Ansicht; aktivierte MouseFollower2D, kinematischen Körper und genau eine aktive Kamera prüfen.
  • Ziele bewegen sich nicht: Dynamic, BoxCollider2D, Gravitation 0 und Ebene 0 ↔ 0 prüfen.
  • Kein Punkt außerhalb der Ansicht: Gruppe exakt knockout-target, laufenden Manager-Timer und API v2 view_min/max prüfen.
  • Doppelte Punkte: Gruppe nur einmal vergeben und kein zweites Punkteskript hinzufügen.
  • Keine Siegesleiste: Namen exakt Congratulations Bar, Congratulations Text, Score Text; remaining entspricht Spawnanzahl.
  • Build fehlt: Desktop-Editor auf Zielhost, Windows-x86-64-Vorlage, Startszene und fehlerfreies Project Health erforderlich.
Nova_A 6.0.1 · complete playable project · world-space pointer physics

从项目到便携游戏：制作“鼠标击退”

这是一套可照着完成并运行的准确流程，不是面板名称列表。内置模板已经实现完整游戏；本文还讲解如何检查、修改、重建、测试与导出。

Nova_A 现在能否真正制作游戏

可以。Nova_A 能制作并运行本游戏：使用确定性固定步长 2D 物理，读取鼠标／键盘／手柄输入，运行时生成预制体，执行 Rhai 或可视化图表逻辑，更新 UI，并导出独立播放器。

在 Windows 上，只要安装了匹配的 Windows 播放器模板且“项目健康”通过，Nova_A 桌面编辑器就能打包便携的 x86-64 .exe。浏览器版编辑器可以构建网页文件夹，但浏览器无法编译原生 .exe。代码签名与全新电脑验证仍需发布者单独完成。

1. 创建可直接游玩的项目

  1. 启动 Nova_A 桌面编辑器，选择 新建项目（New Project）。
  2. 输入项目名称（例如 Mouse Knockout），选择可写的空文件夹，在模板中选择 鼠标击退。
  3. 选择 创建项目（Create Project）。系统将 Mouse Knockout Arena 设为启动场景，并显示 Assets/Tutorials/Getting Started.md。
  4. 先保存一次，建立可靠的项目文档，再开始修改或构建。

2. 修改前先验证完整游戏

  1. 在运行工具栏选择 播放（Play）。
  2. 把鼠标移入游戏视图。蓝色方块会按摄像机世界坐标跟随指针；缩放、DPI 与宽高比不会改变物理单位。
  3. 撞击八个橙色目标，把它们推出画面。目标中心越过摄像机边界和安全余量后才计分。
  4. 确认分数依次从 Score 1 / 8 到 8 / 8，随后出现 Congratulations! All targets cleared. 提示条。
  5. 选择 停止（Stop）。运行时变化会被丢弃，场景和资源的创作数据保持不变。

3. 理解模板中的每个对象与设置

  • Main Camera：启用的 Camera2D，正交尺寸 10，深色背景。
  • Mouse Player：矩形渲染、Kinematic RigidBody2D、BoxCollider2D、弹性 0.7、低摩擦，并使用原生 MouseFollower2D；最大速度 40 可保持快速响应并限制碰撞冲量，0 是可选的无限制模式。
  • Game Manager：生成八个目标，按定时器检查摄像机边界，管理分数和胜利 UI。
  • Game HUD：屏幕空间 Canvas，参考尺寸 1920 × 1080。
  • Score Text / Instruction Text：运行分数与操作提示。
  • Congratulations Bar / Congratulations Text：开始时禁用，只在 8 / 8 时启用。
  • Knockout Target.nova-prefab：Dynamic RigidBody2D、弹性 0.86、低摩擦、BoxCollider2D、分组 knockout-target。
  • 场景物理：重力 0、固定频率 60 Hz、启用插值；碰撞层 0 与层 0 交互。

4. 自己绘制或替换对象

  1. 停止播放，打开 设计（Design），选择 矩形（Rectangle） 绘制工具，在场景视图拖动；拖动范围就是实际世界宽高。
  2. 在层级中选择新对象，在检查器重命名并设置 Transform2D，确认存在 ShapeRenderer2D 与 BoxCollider2D。
  3. 若替换玩家：将 RigidBody2D → Body type 设为 Kinematic，Gravity scale 设为 0，摩擦设低，再添加 MouseFollower2D；Offset 保持 0, 0、最大速度设为 40，可得到快速且有界的碰撞；只有明确需要无限制速度时才设为 0。新对象通过播放测试后再禁用或删除原玩家。
  4. 若替换目标：使用 Dynamic、Gravity scale 0、约 0.86 弹性和低摩擦，并加入 knockout-target 分组；目标不需要单独脚本。
  5. 选中目标，在检查器选择 创建预制体（Create Prefab）；从资源面板复制 asset://GUID，替换管理器脚本中的 TARGET_PREFAB_GUID。
  6. 目标尺寸建议约 1.25 × 1.25；生成中心必须位于 Camera2D 画面内。

5. 理解自动指针组件并编辑管理器脚本

MouseFollower2D 在原生固定物理步中读取活动游戏视图的世界坐标指针并设置运动速度；无需每帧运行脚本，也能保留碰撞响应。

KnockoutGameManager.rhai 管理生成、边界检测、销毁、分数和 UI。它每 50 毫秒检查一次分组目标，因此无需为每个目标运行相同脚本。模板包含八条完整 spawn_at；下方是契约的缩略示例。

@export(type="int", min=1, max=64, step=1, group="Game") let remaining = 8;
fn start() {
  score_set(0.0);
  entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Bar"), false);
  entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Text"), false);
  ui_set_text_on(find_entity_handle("Score Text"), "Score  0 / 8");
  spawn_at("asset://TARGET_PREFAB_GUID", -6.0, -3.8, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);
  // Repeat spawn_at at the seven other authored positions.
  timer_start("bounds", 0.05, true);
}
fn on_timer(name) {
  if name != "bounds" || remaining <= 0 { return; }
  let margin = 0.8;
  for target in query_group("knockout-target", 16) {
    let x = entity_position_x_on(target);
    let y = entity_position_y_on(target);
    if x < view_min_x() - margin || x > view_max_x() + margin
      || y < view_min_y() - margin || y > view_max_y() + margin {
      entity_destroy(target); score_add(1.0); remaining = remaining - 1;
    }
  }
  ui_set_text_on(find_entity_handle("Score Text"), `Score  ${8 - remaining} / 8`);
  if remaining == 0 {
    timer_cancel("bounds");
    entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Bar"), true);
    entity_set_enabled(find_entity_handle("Congratulations Text"), true);
  }
}

6. 发布前配置检查表

  • 项目设置 → 物理：固定频率 60 Hz，本场景重力 0，启用插值。
  • 碰撞矩阵：玩家与目标所在层的交互必须启用；UI 对象不应有物理碰撞器。
  • 输入：读取指针无需创建动作；mouse_world_x/y 直接读取活动游戏视图。键盘／手柄仍通过输入映射配置。
  • 摄像机：只启用一个游戏 Camera2D；正交尺寸与视口决定 view_min/max_x/y。
  • 构建设置：运行模式 Game，启动场景 Mouse Knockout Arena，目标 Windows，架构 x86_64，启用 Package into executable，标识符如 top.whitelists.mouseknockout，版本 1.0.0。
  • 项目健康：构建前解决全部“错误”；签名或外部全新电脑证据的警告不会改变游戏逻辑。

7. 构建便携 Windows 游戏

  1. 保存项目，打开 管理 → 项目健康（Manage → Project Health） 并运行验证。
  2. 打开 管理 → 构建设置 → 概览（Manage → Build Settings → Overview）。
  3. 选择 Windows、x86_64、运行模式 Game、Portable application / Package into executable。
  4. 在场景列表加入 Mouse Knockout Arena，放到第一项并设为 Startup。
  5. 测试选择 Development，发布选择 Release；保持确定性打包开启。
  6. 选择项目源目录以外的输出文件夹，然后点击 构建并运行（Build & Run）。
  7. Nova_A 会生成游戏数据、调用匹配的本地播放器模板、写出并启动 .exe。之后应复制到另一台 Windows x86-64 电脑完成全新环境验证。
  8. 若构建网页：选择 Web 和 Web player folder，通过 HTTP(S) 提供完整输出文件夹；不要用 file:// 直接打开 index.html。

8. 常见失败与准确修复方法

  • 玩家不动：鼠标必须位于游戏视图；确认 MouseFollower2D 已启用、刚体为 Kinematic，且只有一个活动摄像机。
  • 目标不动：确认 Dynamic、BoxCollider2D、重力 0，并启用碰撞层 0 ↔ 0。
  • 出界但不加分：确认分组严格为 knockout-target、管理器定时器正在运行、API v2 提供 view_min/max。
  • 重复加分：目标只加入一次分组，不要再添加第二套计分脚本。
  • 胜利条不出现：名称必须严格为 Congratulations Bar、Congratulations Text、Score Text；remaining 必须等于生成数量。
  • 无法构建：必须使用目标系统上的桌面编辑器，安装并验证 Windows x86-64 导出模板，设置启动场景并清除项目健康错误。

Nova_A 6.2 behavior contracts

Open a Rhai asset in Script → Script Studio → Contract. Existing scripts need no change. Add contract header inserts strict/deterministic intent and bounded commands/logs. Add // @requires component, input, asset, or package only when the behavior truly depends on it. The page explains API thread, determinism, and permissions. Play, Project Health, and Build use the same diagnostics; repair the named dependency and save. Graph↔Rhai synchronization and Project Format 2/schema 29 remain unchanged.

Nova_A 5.0.1 editor organization

All 5.0 commands, shortcuts, workflows, animations and persisted contracts remain. Workspaces, transforms, history and simulation stay direct; Layout, Commands, Authoring tools and View settings expose the complete secondary command set in named keyboard-accessible groups. The scene toolbar no longer relies on horizontal scrolling. A 12 px caption and 13 px dense-control floor, clearer surfaces, role colors and responsive popovers are qualified across English, German and Chinese, both themes and reduced motion.

Nova_A 5.0 frozen baseline

Project Format 2 schema 29, Rhai API 2, Plugin API 2, Package Manifest 1, Build CLI 1, Workspace document 3 and the eleven-file release format are frozen. New scripts use API v2; imported API v1 remains read-only migration compatibility. Windows and Web are Tier 1; Experimental targets are not shown in default release authoring. A local candidate is not final certification until the real soak, observation, clean-machine, browser, reproducibility, signing, tagged-source and independent-verifier gates are attached.

Nova_A 5.0 first game

Create a Platformer project, run tests and Play/Stop, resolve Project Health, then export Windows and Web Tier-1 presets. Release exports use provenance, SBOM and deployment headers. Serve Web through HTTP(S), never file://. See docs/FIRST_GAME_5_0.md.

Project Health warnings

Open the affected editor, repair references, validate and canonicalize before saving, review package/build/script/UI failures, and preserve a backup before migration. Every warning remains actionable and no repair silently removes content. See docs/TROUBLESHOOTING_5_0.md.

Script Studio diagnostics

Problems reports stable codes, source positions, phases and code actions. New projects use Rhai API v2. API v1 is displayed only on an imported v1 asset as a disabled compatibility state; migrate the calls to v2 and re-run tests.

Migration and rollback

Schemas 5–29 migrate in memory, validate, rerun deterministically and commit only after backup. Workspace v2 migrates to v3. Downgrade is not promised; use the backup/source revision. See docs/MIGRATION_5_0.md.

Package & Plugin SDK

Package Manifest 1 and Plugin API 2 are frozen. Installation verifies registry policy, publisher, license, provenance, hashes, signature, compatibility, dependencies, certification and permissions before execution. Safe Mode skips third-party startup. See docs/PACKAGE_PLUGIN_SDK_5_0.md.

Build and export warnings

Fix target, host, identifier, version, startup scene, deterministic/profile, content, provenance and deployment diagnostics before output. Hooks never run implicitly. See docs/BUILD_EXPORT_5_0.md.

Platform support

Windows x86-64 editor/player and Web player are Tier 1. Linux/macOS are Experimental matching-host records and Android is unavailable. See docs/PLATFORM_BUILD_MATRIX_5_0.md.

Security and diagnostics privacy

Packages fail closed. Diagnostic/crash bundles stay local and are never uploaded automatically; review optional identifiers/paths and exclude secrets and signing material. See docs/SECURITY_POLICY_5_0.md.

Localization and accessibility

Resolve missing localized strings, overflow, direction, accessible-name, focus, target-size and contrast failures before Stable output. Test English, German, Chinese, DPI, keyboard and reduced motion. See docs/ACCESSIBILITY_GUIDE_5_0.md.

Troubleshooting

Use Safe Layout/Safe Mode, Project Health, package rollback, privacy-reviewed diagnostics and clean reference projects. Never force-open a newer project in an older editor. See docs/TROUBLESHOOTING_5_0.md.

Build, release and certification

The unified pipeline creates eleven artifacts and local evidence, while 72-hour soak, 14-day observation, two-machine reproducibility, clean lifecycle, external browsers/hardware, signing and independent verification remain pending until executed. See docs/RELEASE_ENGINEERING_5_0.md.

Nova_A 4.8 rendering, audio and performance

Rendering reports the real path, device, driver, API, extensions, limits, feature matrix, fallback reason, texture/draw budgets and batch breaks. Materials expose typed uniforms, includes, compilation/platform validation and visible fallback. Reusable particles include curves, gradients, collision, subemitters, preview and budgets.

Audio uses a real bus/effect/send/snapshot/automation graph, limiter, semantic peak/RMS/dB/clipping meters, bounded voices, playlists/fades/seek/positioning, output-device hot plug and recovery. Profiler captures include markers, counters, annotations, renderer/audio/particle snapshots, comparison and CI budgets; Health and Build consume the same failures.

Nova_A 4.7 animation and runtime UI

Animation provides eight production track types, per-key interpolation, retime/ripple/reduce/slice tools, state layers/transitions/blends/runtime inspection, 2D rigs, attachments, retarget aliases, import compression and sampling validation. Controls remain disabled until an animation asset is selected.

UI shares hierarchy, selection and Inspector; supports responsive anchors, containers, breakpoints, safe areas, clipping, scrolling, z-order, reusable variants and six device presets. Themes cover all token families. Localization adds CSV/PO, plurals, fallback, formatting, pseudo, RTL/Bidi and font fallback. Semantic accessibility, focus, contrast, reduced motion, captions and automatic keyboard/mouse/gamepad/touch prompts are checked in Project Health and Build Settings.

Nova_A 4.6 complete programming workflow

Script Studio now has Explorer, multi-file Editor and dockable Problems/Tests/Debug roles. Semantic completion, signatures, hover, diagnostics, symbols, Definition, References, Rename, code actions, formatting, module help and an atomic persisted index use project-owned format and lint settings. Rhai API v2 documents 110 entries with module, lifetime, thread, determinism, permission and migration metadata; imported API v1 assets keep their adapter.

Persistent grouped breakpoints, stack/frame selection, locals, watches, exceptions, tasks and callback-safe stepping join loopback-only authenticated exported-player policy. Hot reload compiles and classifies before transactional apply, retains state-transfer history and rollback, and never replaces a valid program with a failed candidate. Seven test categories support tags, fixtures, cases, setup/teardown, timeout, cancellation, seed, JSON/JUnit/coverage, changed selection, shards and stable CLI exits.

Nova_A 4.5 production 2D physics

Project-scoped Accurate, Balanced, Fast and Custom profiles control fixed rate, catch-up, interpolation, dropped time, substeps, solver iterations and sleep. Structured ray, point, overlap, sweep, nearest and contact APIs use named physics layers. Distance, revolute, prismatic, weld, spring, motor and Rope2D expose anchors, limits, damping, connected collision, break thresholds and telemetry. The virtual Physics Monitor sorts and pins bodies, draws speed history, shows collision/joint/Rope details, exports captures and compares snapshots. The Assets toolbar keeps daily import/create actions and moves Export Folder to •••. Grid/list, search, tags, favorites, collections, saved filters and an incremental window support large projects. The Asset Importer separates Source, Import, Dependencies, Provenance and Platform Overrides. Sprite import covers color/filter/mipmap/compression/transparency/PPU, pivot, trim, grid/automatic slicing, nine-slice, polygon/collision, animation extraction, deterministic atlas and SVG. Nova_A 4.3 production authoring

Loaded-scene tabs expose dirty, external, validation, and prefab state plus history, templates, runtime policy, inheritance, tags, named layers, and dependency inspection. Hierarchy rows are virtualized for 10,000 objects and support search, type/tag/saved filters, pins, selection Back/Forward, breadcrumbs, isolation, visibility, locks, range selection, reparenting, and reorder.

Nova_A 4.2 project integrity

Every authored edit uses central named/grouped undo history and consistent dirty state. Save validates and canonicalizes, journals affected files and checksums, stages and verifies temporary output, then commits; interruption never promotes recovery data over the last manual save. Recovery Browser and external-change dialogs always require an explicit preview/compare and restore, discard, copy, disk, or editor choice.

Nova_A 4.1 modern editor

Design, Script, Animation, UI, Debug and Manage are the six public workspaces. The left rail is contextual; Manage owns Settings, Packages, Project Health, Rendering and Build. Nova_A 4.0 production baseline

Every external project receives a compatibility preflight before open. Supported 3.x upgrades require a complete source download, retain a local rollback record, migrate in memory through the Rust registry, validate and canonicalize the entire document, and only then replace the session. Project Format 2 schema 29, Runtime API 1, Plugin API 2, Package Manifest 1 and Build CLI 1 are locked for compatible 4.0.x patches.

Studio Status declares Stable, Beta and Development channels, carries the offline known-issues feed, and creates diagnostics only after privacy review. Nova_A 3.5 Rhai API v1 and Script workspace

Script now combines project files, tabs, breakpoints, Find/Replace, semantic completion, parameter help and unsaved recovery with separate Problems, Outline, Debug, Tests, API, Modules and Signals pages. Format, Definition, References and Rename use the project symbol index. Complete API · External editor protocol.

Nova_A 3.4 production 2D physics

Project Settings → Physics owns fixed simulation, interpolation, units, 32 named/color-coded collision layers, compact pairs/full matrix, material assets and conformance. Materials bind density, friction, restitution, thresholds and combine rules to native calculations. Collider2D exposes box, circle, capsule, segment, chain and convex/concave polygons with visible support status plus local compound shapes.

Stable collision and trigger Enter/Stay/Exit events join ray, shape, point, overlap and contact queries, teleport and move-and-slide APIs. Character floor/wall/ceiling, slopes, steps, floor snap, moving platforms and safe margin have overlays. Seven joint types expose limits, motors, break thresholds and diagnostics. Profiler records CCD, sleeping bodies, joints, contacts and fixed-step health; replay, reference scenes, tunnelling, determinism, character, performance, stacking and soak evidence ship with the release.

1. Quick start

  1. Start Nova_A and choose a Project Manager template, or open a .nova/JSON project.
  2. Create entities in Scene, add components in the Object Inspector and configure named actions in Settings.
  3. Play in Game view; Pause and Step diagnose fixed physics. Stop restores the edit snapshot.
  4. Save the project, order scenes in Build Settings, choose startup/target and Build.

One entered world unit equals one grid unit. Runtime and editor state are deliberately isolated.

2. Project Manager

ControlAction
Open ProjectValidates and opens while retaining project UUID.
Import ProjectOpens as a copy with a new UUID.
Continue ProjectReturns to the project cached before the manager.
Create ProjectCreates and audits Empty 2D, Platformer, Top-down or Physics Sandbox.
Recent entry / ×Opens a local snapshot or removes only the history entry.
Language / Manual / GitHubChanges locale or opens local help/source.

Empty supplies Camera2D. Platformer proves sprite, animation, input, script, physics, tilemap, audio and HUD. Top-down proves prefab spawning, patrol AI, triggers, scene changes, particles and saves. Physics Sandbox proves materials, a joint and a physical rope.

3. Every editor command

File

Project Manager caches and returns home; Save Project/Ctrl+S saves the editable document; Import Project migrates/validates; Clear Scene uses the Nova confirmation and remains undoable.

Edit

Undo/Redo, Copy/Paste/Duplicate (new UUIDs), Rename/F2, Delete, Deselect/Escape. Destructive actions use the in-app dialog, never browser confirm.

View and Help

Grid is independent from X/Y axes. Reset Camera restores pan/zoom. Console, Profiler, Project and Build open bottom tools. Help opens this manual or GitHub.

Pages and tools

Scene edits; Game displays Camera2D/runtime UI; Settings configures experience and project systems. Select/Shift/marquee, move/rotate/scale gizmos and rectangle/ellipse/triangle drawing are undoable. Short exit clicks are suppressed. Play starts, Pause freezes, Step advances one fixed tick, Stop restores.

4. Scene, workspaces, hierarchy, layers and inspector

Design, Script, Animation, Interface and Debug workspaces rearrange existing tools. H/I/B independently toggle Hierarchy, Inspector and the bottom drawer; Focus Mode hides them temporarily. Layout choices remain local and Reset Layout restores Design. Ctrl/Cmd+K or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P opens a keyboard-navigable command palette for every workspace, view, bottom tool and layout action.

Hierarchy search filters names; expansion shows children. Reparenting uses Transform2D UUIDs and rejects cycles. Visible/locked/enabled are distinct. Scenes can be created, renamed, duplicated, loaded, unloaded, deleted and activated; runtime loads by UUID or name and retains persistent entities.

Editor/render layers and physics layers are separate. Collision requires mutual layer/mask permission; connections require the same editor layer. The sticky Inspector search and category chips filter metadata/components without disabling them. Add Component opens a searchable categorized picker. Transform2D is mandatory; unique components cannot duplicate. Component tools enable, copy, paste, reset and remove.

The Add UI area creates Canvas, Panel, Image, Text, Button, Slider, ProgressBar, Checkbox and TextInput. Parent Canvas, readable sizes and positions are automatic. UI renders/selects in Scene and Game; images have missing placeholders; Game text input supports IME, paste, multiline and passwords.

5. Stable Component API 2.0

GroupComponents and contract
CoreTransform2D: local position, radians rotation, scale, parent. Every component has persistent UUID, enabled/removed.
RenderCamera2D active/ortho/zoom/background/pixel-perfect/viewport/range; SpriteRenderer2D image/tint/opacity/size/pivot/flips/sorting/material/filter; ShapeRenderer2D geometry/fill/stroke/texture; TextRenderer2D world text/font/style; ParticleEmitter2D bounded emission/lifetime/velocity/color/texture.
PhysicsRigidBody2D; BoxCollider2D, EllipseCollider2D (equal radii = circle), PolygonCollider2D; Fixed, Distance, Revolute, Prismatic, SpringJoint2D; Rope2D.
GameplayScript2D Rhai/properties/errors; Animator controller/state/parameters; AudioSource clip/mix/spatial and AudioListener.
UICanvas, RectTransform, Panel, Image, Text, Button, Slider, ProgressBar, Checkbox, TextInput.
WorldTileMap2D: TileSet, dimensions, tile/chunk size, cells and collision.

6. Physics

Persistent Rust PhysicsWorld uses a fixed timestep, so render refresh rate does not alter results. Dynamic bodies integrate forces/impulses; kinematic bodies follow velocity and transfer motion; static bodies stay fixed. Automatic mass is density × area and inertia is analytic. Damping is timestep-independent. Friction may exceed one; restitution threshold controls low-speed bounce.

Sensors report enter/stay/exit without impulses. One-way platforms block one side. Continuous mode uses adaptive substeps. Sleeping wakes on relevant changes. Raycast/all, overlap point/shape and shape casts honor masks. Rendering and collision geometry never imply each other.

7. Connections, joints and binding

Choose exactly two same-layer objects, Straight or Manual, then drag between center/surface/side/vertex anchors. Center markers are blue rings with white dots. Stretch, bend, stiffness, damping, maximum strain, bend/stretch load, thickness, density and collision are runtime values.

Straight lines repatch between moving/resized anchors. Manual paths deform as sampled rope. Ropes exclude the two attached bodies but may collide with others; impacts travel to anchors and bodies. Overload breaks the correct link and fragments continue. Overlapping objects can Bind into a compound with removed internal outline, shared drag, combined mass/inertia/collision; Separate reverses it.

8. Renderer and assets

The Rendering tool exposes five passes; Point/Spot/Directional/Area Light2D; masks, ambient and normal-mapped lighting; ShadowCaster2D; safe GLSL ES materials; camera stacks, viewports and render textures; optional effects; debug views; GPU/pass statistics; and PNG captures. Only a custom post material allocates the optional framebuffer; Canvas2D remains fallback.

Sprite and UI Image support nine-slice. Imports preserve atlas/filter, sRGB/Linear and platform compression variants. Assets use persistent asset://UUID references.

9. Input and scripting API

Input actions are Button, Axis or Vector2; bindings cover keyboard, mouse/button/wheel and gamepad button/axis with scale, vector contribution, pad index and deadzone.

Lifecycles: awake, start, fixed_update(dt), update(dt), late_update(dt), on_destroy, on_timer, collision enter/stay/exit and trigger enter/exit. Export with @export let speed = 5.0;.

Read: entity/name/find/has/get component, transform, rigid_body, animator, audio_source, time functions, input down/pressed/released/axis/vector, mouse/wheel. Commands: apply force/impulse; set velocity/position/rotation/scale/angular velocity; animator parameters/play; audio play/pause/stop; instantiate/destroy; scene load/reload/quit; timer start/pause/resume/cancel; Save APIs.

The Rhai sandbox has no filesystem, network, process, DOM, eval/import. Operation/call/depth limits stop runaway scripts; one error disables/logs that instance without crashing the engine.

10. Animation, audio, UI, tilemaps, particles and prefabs

AnimationClip has exact sprite-frame durations/property keys. AnimatorController has typed parameters, states and conditional transitions. Audio uses Master/Music/SFX/UI buses, sample rate, AudioListener and spatial blend/ranges. Canvas/RectTransform UI dispatches hover, press, click, slider drag, checkbox and native text; ProgressBar is display-only. TileMap palette paints/erases/picks/fills chunked tiles with None/Box/Polygon/OneWay collision. Particles use bounded deterministic pools.

Prefabs store entity subtrees, source UUIDs and instance overrides. Apply updates only non-overridden values; Revert clears overrides; missing sources stay diagnosable. Runtime instantiation waits for a safe structural phase.

11. Console, profiler and debugger

Console levels are Trace, Debug, Info, Warning, Error, Fatal with text, category and source filters. Categories include Engine, Runtime, Physics, Script, Asset, Build, Save and Plugin. Profiler tracks frame/physics/scripts/render/animation/audio/assets, FPS, bodies, draw calls and memory over 180 samples; Freeze/Clear control it. Physics overlays show colliders, AABBs, contacts, normals, joints, rope nodes and sleeping bodies without changing simulation. Crash logging records fatal failures where supported.

12. Save-game API

Save data is isolated by project UUID + slot and separate from project/scene files. Values: finite number, boolean, string, null, arrays and maps. Use save_has, save_get, save_set, save_delete, save_clear, save_load(slot), save_commit(slot). Settings can inspect/load/commit/clear. Limits: 1 MB, depth 8, 2,000 items per collection.

13. WASM Plugin API 1

Import manifest + matching WASM. Manifest requires reverse-domain ID, name, SemVer, API 1, engine range, safe entry, enabled and only log/events permissions. Required exports: nova_plugin_api_version() == 1, nova_plugin_init(); optional update/shutdown. No filesystem/process/network, maximum 16 MB. Invalid plugins are rejected; a trap disables it for that play session.

14. Build and export

Set game name, Windows/Linux/macOS/Web, x86_64, ordered scenes, startup scene, development build, output and optional Windows/Linux single executable. Default is Player + game.nova-pak; Build & Run starts native output. The pack uses a versioned header/index, safe relative paths, GUID/type, offsets, compressed/original lengths, gzip and SHA-256. Desktop targets build on matching OS; Web is static. Player contains no editor UI.

Animation Studio, rigging and Timeline

Clip assets open a dope sheet and curve editor with multi-target tracks, box/multi-selection, snapping, copy/paste and Auto/Linear/Constant/Free tangents. Record mode writes Inspector and gizmo transforms. Controllers provide conditions, exit time, interruption, weighted/additive layers, masks, subgraphs and 1D blend trees. Skeleton2D combines rig bones, pose overrides, IK, constraints and weighted inverse-bind skins. TimelinePlayer runs Animation, Audio, Camera, Event, Visibility and ScriptCall tracks at deterministic fixed ticks. Animation events use signals. Asset reimport maps and resamples a source clip while keeping the target GUID.

15. Worlds and gameplay tools

World Tools contains CharacterBody2D, Area2D effectors, optional Navigation and AI packages, WorldChunk2D streaming, portals and prefab object pools. Character motion uses exact Rust world units with slopes, steps, moving platforms, one-way surfaces and coyote helpers. Tilemap supports palettes, brush/terrain assets, layers and collision/navigation/occluder bake reports. See the English Markdown manual for every field and runtime signal.

16. Compatibility and release audit

Nova_A Project Format 2 uses schema 22 and supports legacy schema 5+. Files contain format/major/schema/engine/compatibility/project UUID. Schema 22 validates platform/delivery settings while preserving production, presentation, audio, world and unknown asset data. Ordered migrations preserve IDs, components, hierarchy, scenes, assets, prefabs, input/audio, tiles/particles/joints and build data. Newer unknown formats are rejected.

Audit: test every Presentation, World Tools and Production Lab tab; UI controls/focus/locales/mixer; replay/tests/data/jobs/networking; tile layers and bakes; save/reopen; Play/Pause/Step/Stop; game/headless builds; confirm unused optional resources/locales/networking are stripped.

16. Three complete tutorials

Physics playground

Create Physics Sandbox, tune body materials, run, inspect DistanceJoint/rope, enable physical rope collision and debug overlays, then overload it and observe simulated fragments.

Platformer

Inspect exported speed/jump, sprite, Animator assets and jump audio. Review MoveHorizontal/Jump, paint TileMap, adjust platforms/camera/HUD, play with A/D + Space, add a scene and export.

Top-down

WASD moves; E spawns the enemy prefab. Inspect patrol/particles. Enter Exit Trigger to commit checkpoint and load Main Menu. Load slot1, edit prefab while preserving overrides, then build both scenes.

17. Shortcuts and troubleshooting

Ctrl/Cmd+S save; Z undo; Shift+Z or Y redo; C/V/D copy/paste/duplicate; Delete remove; F2 rename; Escape cancel. Invisible: check enabled, scene/layer, camera, sorting, asset. No collision: check colliders, body types, physics layers/masks, sensor. Script: use Console source, action names, export types. Build: valid ordered/startup scenes and matching host OS. Never hand-edit a failed legacy schema; preserve original and report the migration error.

18. Script Studio 2.2

The Script workspace is a full-width Rhai IDE with project/source search, tabs, line gutter, breakpoints, find/replace, completion, signature and hover context, symbols, definitions, safe rename, diagnostics, modules, debugger, tests, signals and a generated Engine API. Valid saves hot-reload cached bytecode at a safe frame boundary; invalid edits keep the prior program. Read-only use modules reject missing/circular dependencies. Typed handles return valid/kind/id/error. Entity-owned tasks and the shared physics/UI/animation/scene signal queue are lifetime-safe. Release builds strip debug metadata unless Development Build is enabled.

19. Presentation: UI, Audio, localization and Accessibility

UI: Canvas/RectTransform/Panel apply anchors, fixed/fill/content policies, min/max, aspect, safe areas, responsive breakpoints, horizontal/vertical/grid containers, clipping, rounded masks, wheel scrolling and reusable UI prefabs. Theme assets inherit parents and variables, provide control states and allow style-class/per-control overrides.

Accessibility: Tab/arrows/D-pad navigate visible focus; explicit direction UUIDs override spatial lookup. Buttons can capture input remaps. Role, label and description export to the Game screen-reader tree. Runtime accessibility stays separate from editor preferences.

Localization: tables support locale fallback, plural/select maps, variables, number/date formatting, pseudo, font fallback, RTL and live preview. Builds retain only source plus selected locales.

Audio: the bounded graph has buses, parents, sends, mute/solo, wet/dry effects, meters, snapshots, ducking, spatial curves, streaming and voice limits. Assets expose waveform, loop markers and normalization; diagnostics split active/streaming/buffered/limited voices. Help opens this manual inside the same-origin editor overlay, never through the external opener.

20. Production Lab, tests, data and optional networking

Trace/Memory: bounded frame traces correlate input, scripts, animation, physics, audio, render, asset work, allocations and GPU passes. Capture/Compare, memory budgets, lifetime views and leak candidates are diagnostic and never delete project data.

Replay/Tests: Record stores normalized fixed-step input, seeded random state and physics checksums; Play restores the initial project and reports exact mismatches. Unit, Scene, Integration and Headless tests support assertions, tolerance, timeout, step limits, optional screenshots and JSON/JUnit output.

Data/Jobs: Data Schema/Table assets validate typed rows, import CSV/JSON/external database result arrays and generate TypeScript accessors. Versioned saves apply ordered migrations. Worker queues and fallback execution are bounded and cancellable.

Networking/Build: official WebSocket/native-UDP networking is uninstalled, disabled and stripped by default. Once installed it exposes lifecycle, RPC, replication, snapshots, interpolation, prediction/rollback, budgets and diagnostics. Authoritative headless mode requires native output plus enabled networking. WebGL multisampling, high-quality Canvas smoothing and font optical shaping improve anti-aliasing while Nearest pixel art stays crisp.

Vollständige 2D-Spiele bauen und veröffentlichen.

Offline-Referenz für Authoring, Laufzeit, Pakete, Zusammenarbeit, Build und Release.

Nova_A 6.2 Verhaltensverträge

Öffne Rhai unter Skript → Script Studio → Vertrag. Alte Skripte bleiben gültig. Der Vertragskopf beschreibt strikte/deterministische Ausführung, Voraussetzungen sowie Befehls-/Log-Budgets. Die Seite erklärt Thread-Regeln, Determinismus und Berechtigungen. Play, Projektzustand und Build verwenden dieselben Fehler; behebe die genannte Voraussetzung und speichere. Graph↔Rhai und Schema 29 bleiben unverändert.

Nova_A 5.0.1 – Editororganisation

Alle 5.0-Befehle, Kürzel, Arbeitsabläufe, Animationen und Datenverträge bleiben erhalten. Arbeitsbereiche, Transformation, Verlauf und Simulation bleiben direkt; Layout, Befehle, Werkzeuge und Ansichtseinstellungen enthalten den vollständigen sekundären Befehlssatz in benannten, tastaturbedienbaren Gruppen. Die Szenenleiste benötigt kein horizontales Scrollen mehr. Mindestschriftgrößen von 12/13 px, deutlichere Flächen, Rollenfarben und responsive Popover werden in Englisch, Deutsch und Chinesisch geprüft.

Nova_A 5.0 Produktionsbasis

Schema 29, Rhai API 2, Plugin API 2, Paketmanifest 1, Build CLI 1 und Workspace-Dokument 3 sind eingefroren. Neue Skripte verwenden v2; v1 bleibt nur zur Migration lesbar. Windows/Web sind Tier 1. Die lokale Ausgabe bleibt bis zu Soak, Beobachtung, zwei Rechnern, Clean-Machine, Browser/Hardware, Signatur und unabhängiger Prüfung ein Kandidat.

Nova_A 4.9 Build, Pakete und Release

Windows/Web sind Tier 1; Linux/macOS bleiben Experimental auf passendem Host; Mobil ist ausdrücklich nicht verfügbar. Pakete werden vor Ausführung nach Registry, Herausgeber, Lizenz, Provenienz, Hash, Signatur, API und Berechtigungen geprüft. Teamfunktionen sind optional und lokal. Die Pipeline erzeugt elf Artefakte und führt externe Signatur-, Clean-Machine-, Browser- und 14-Tage-RC-Gates ehrlich auf.

Nova_A 4.8 – Rendering, Audio und Leistung

Rendering zeigt Pfad, Gerät, Treiber, API, Erweiterungen, Grenzen, Funktionsmatrix, Fallback, Textur-/Draw-Budgets und Batch-Gründe. Materialien besitzen Uniforms, Includes, Compiler-/Plattformprüfung und sichtbaren Fallback. Partikelsysteme bieten Kurven, Verläufe, Kollision, Subemitter, Vorschau und Budgets.

Audio verwendet Busse, Effekte, Sends, Snapshots, Automation, Limiter und Peak/RMS/dB/Clipping-Anzeigen sowie Geräte-Hot-Plug und Wiederherstellung. Profiler-Captures enthalten Marker, Zähler, Anmerkungen, Vergleiche und CI-Budgets; Projektzustand und Build verwenden dieselben Fehler.

Nova_A 4.7 – Animation und Runtime-UI

Animation bietet acht Spurtypen, Interpolation, Zeitwerkzeuge, Zustands-Layer/Übergänge/Blends, Laufzeitinspektion, 2D-Rigs, Anhänge, Retargeting, Importkompression und Sampling-Prüfung. Ohne ausgewählten Clip bleiben Werkzeuge deaktiviert.

UI teilt Hierarchie, Auswahl und Inspektor und bietet responsive Anker, Container, Breakpoints, Safe Areas, Clipping, Scrollen, Z-Reihenfolge, Varianten und sechs Geräte. Theme, Lokalisierung, RTL/Bidi, Font-Fallback, Semantik, Fokus, Kontrast, reduzierte Bewegung, Untertitel und automatische Eingabehinweise sind integriert.

Nova_A 4.6 – vollständiger Programmierablauf

Script Studio trennt Explorer, Mehrdatei-Editor und andockbare Probleme/Tests/Debug-Details. Semantische Vervollständigung, Signaturen, Hover, Diagnose, Symbole, Definition, Referenzen, Umbenennen, Codeaktionen, Formatierung, Modulhilfe und ein atomar gespeicherter Index verwenden Projekteinstellungen. Rhai API v2 dokumentiert 110 Einträge; importierte v1-Assets behalten ihren Adapter und erhalten Migrationsdiagnosen.

Gruppierte Breakpoints, Stack/Frame, Lokale, Watches, Ausnahmen, Tasks und sichere Schritte ergänzen lokal authentifiziertes Player-Debugging. Hot Reload kompiliert und klassifiziert vor der Transaktion, bewahrt Verlauf/Rollback und ersetzt ein gültiges Programm nie durch einen Fehler. Sieben Testkategorien bieten Tags, Fixtures, Fälle, Setup/Teardown, Timeout, Abbruch, Seeds, JSON/JUnit/Coverage, Shards und stabile CLI-Exitcodes.

Projektprofile steuern feste Rate, Aufholen, Interpolation, Zeitverlust, Teilschritte, Iterationen und Schlaf. Strukturierte Abfragen nutzen benannte Physikschichten. CharacterBody2D trennt Frame-Eingabe und Festschrittbewegung und klassifiziert Boden, Hang, Stufe, Wand, Decke und Plattform.

Gelenke und Rope2D zeigen Anker, Grenzen, Dämpfung, Kollision, Bruch und Telemetrie. Der virtuelle Physics Monitor sortiert, heftet an, zeigt Verlauf, Kollisionen, Constraints und exportierbare Vergleichsaufnahmen. Projektzustand und Overlays melden Budget, verlorene Zeit, Kontakte, Schwerpunkt, Geschwindigkeit und Kraft.

Assets trennt Quelle, Import, Abhängigkeiten, Herkunft und Plattform. Tags, Sammlungen, Filter, Raster/Liste und inkrementelle Fenster navigieren große Projekte. Vollständige Hashes, Importer/Vorgabe/Version/Einstellungen, Cache-Entscheidung, Vergleich, Wiederherstellung und Diagnose sind ausdrücklich sichtbar; ungültige Eingaben erhalten keinen stillen Ersatz.

Sprite-, Atlas-, TileMap-, Kamera-, Parallax-, Spline-Pfad- und Fontabläufe decken die vollständige 2D-Produktion ab, einschließlich Slicing, Kollision, Streaming, deterministischer Speicherung, Pfadfolgern, Shaping, OpenType und Glyphenbericht.

Szenen-Tabs zeigen Ungespeichert-, Extern-, Prüf- und Prefab-Zustand sowie Verlauf, Vorlagen, Laufzeitstrategie, Vererbung, Tags, Ebenen und Abhängigkeiten. Die Hierarchie virtualisiert 10.000 Objekte und bietet Suche, Typ-/Tag-/gespeicherte Filter, Pins, Auswahl Zurück/Vorwärts, Breadcrumbs, Isolation, Sichtbarkeit, Sperre, Bereichsauswahl, Umhängen und Sortieren.

Der Inspektor ergänzt Eigentum/Persistenz, sichere Ausdrücke, gemischte Mehrfachwerte, Pins, Vorgaben und Komponentenprüfung. Prefabs bieten Varianten, Quellnavigation, Konflikte, Verschachtelung/Zyklusschutz und sicheren Ersatz. Ausrichtung, Messung, Kamera-Rahmen, Lineale, Hilfslinien und sieben Snap-Ziele verwenden exakte Einheiten.

Nova_A 4.2 – Projektintegrität

Zentrale Rückgängig-Historie und sichtbarer Ungespeichert-Zustand decken Projektdaten ab. Speichern validiert, kanonisiert, protokolliert, schreibt temporär, prüft und übernimmt atomar; Wiederherstellung überschreibt nie still den manuellen Stand. Externe Änderungen verlangen Vergleich und eine ausdrückliche Datenträger-/Editorwahl.

Schemas 5–29 erhalten Probelauf, Bericht, Backup, Task-Protokoll, Vollprüfung, deterministische Wiederholung und Rollback. Projektzustand bündelt Reparaturvorschau, Referenzzuordnung, Cache, Transaktionen, Wiederherstellung, Migration und Papierkorb.

Nova_A 4.1 – moderner Editor

Design, Skript, Animation, UI, Debug und Verwalten sind die sechs öffentlichen Arbeitsbereiche. Die linke Leiste ist kontextbezogen; Verwalten enthält Einstellungen, Pakete, Projektzustand, Darstellung und Build. Profile, benannte Layouts, Docking, Teilung, schwebende Fenster, Anheften, Auto-Ausblenden, Tab-Sortierung und Reset sind gespeichert.

Lokale variable Schriften bleiben bei DPI-Wechseln scharf. Der Projektmanager prüft eine Vorlage und den Pfad. Debug enthält den Physics Monitor; Verwalten enthält Projektzustand und Build-Bereitschaft. Das Task Center bündelt Fortschritt, Abbruch, Wiederholung, Details, Protokolle und Ressourcen.

Vor dem Öffnen externer Projekte zeigt Nova_A Engine/Schema, Inhalt, Pakete und Migration. Unterstützte 3.x-Projekte erhalten Pflicht-Backup und Rollback, werden im Speicher migriert, vollständig geprüft und erst danach geöffnet. Schema 29 sowie Runtime API 1, Plugin API 2, Package Manifest 1 und Build CLI 1 bleiben in 4.0.x kompatibel.

Studio Status erklärt Stable/Beta/Development, Offline-Probleme und Datenschutz. Absturzpakete sind freiwillige lokale Dateien und werden nie automatisch hochgeladen. Experimentelles Networking bleibt optional und ist keine Stable-Startvorlage.

Der kontextbezogene Tilemap-Editor bietet TileSet-v2-Atlasquellen, Slicing, Animation, Varianten, Terrain und Kachel-Metadaten sowie vollständige Ebenen- und Transformationswerkzeuge. Grid-/Polygon-A*, Radius, Kosten, Masken, Links und Hindernisse teilen dieselben Navigationsdaten. Weltzellen streamen Abhängigkeiten asynchron, abbrechbar und innerhalb des Speicherbudgets. Modal, Popup, Tooltip, Drag/Drop und Scroll laufen in Game. Projektmischung bleibt in Audio.

Barrierefreiheitsmetadaten, Fokus-/Lesereihenfolge, Navigation, Kontrast, reduzierte Bewegung, Textskalierung, Zielgröße und Quellprüfung wirken im Spiel.
